annotation.authors_or_issuer: Gastmans, C.; Sinibaldi, E.; Lerner, R.; Yanez, M.; Kovacs, L.; Palazzani, L. et al.
key_provisions_or_claims: Identifies seven anthropological considerations from Christian anthropology for ethics of socially assistive robots in aged care.
Stresses ontological distinctions between humans and robots, which lack self-reflection, freedom and consciousness.
Robots should support meaningful human relationships rather than estrange humans from them.
Calls for a global, inclusive dialogue including other religious and secular worldviews.
Product of the Pontifical Academy for Life Working Group on Roboethics.
annotation.summary_en: Article by the Pontifical Academy for Life's Working Group on Roboethics presenting seven anthropological considerations from Christian anthropology to guide the ethics of socially assistive robots in older-adult care, emphasizing ontological differences between humans and robots and the value of relationships and human dignity.
annotation.title_clean: Christian anthropology-based contributions to the ethics of socially assistive robots in care for older adults
annotation.title_en: Christian anthropology-based contributions to the ethics of socially assistive robots in care for older adults
